applicable_semantics.rule: when storage_kind = latch, the elements A5FF, B5FF, C5FF, D5FF are not storage elements: their ff_init and ff_srval relations are not applicable (not unknown); sr_kind is not applicable to a latch (its SR is asynchronous)
applicable_semantics.status: a model assumption drawn from docs/ff_latch_probe.md; a changed context is not an illegal configuration

meaning.driven: CE driven from the slice input

clock_mode.basis: the clkinv pair (fdce_inv: IS_C_INVERTED = 1 => bit 0 -> 1) for a flip-flop; for a latch, two host endpoints on the mine site SLICE_X2Y25: the LDCE endpoint of docs/ff_latch_probe.md (CLKINV = 1 with IS_G_INVERTED = 0, bit 1 = not inverted) and the D1' pair of evidence/b4/unit_d1prime_latch_ginv_attempt2_2026_10_18/probe_report.json (IS_G_INVERTED = 1 on the four main LDCE clears CLKINV to 0 with LATCH kept and no other same-class mover, bit 0 = inverted) — host build / readback / bitstream correspondence for one recipe under Vivado 2025.2, not a certificate and not silicon; the bit-0 reading is carried from that one pair to every latch assignment by the named generalisation assumptions G1-G6 of the project_decode_assumption source, and the gate behaviour it implies is the vendor's simulation model (LDCE.v, G_in = G xor IS_G_INVERTED)

meaning.inverted: IS_C_INVERTED = 1: the physical clock is the slice clock inverted; for a latch, IS_G_INVERTED = 1: the gate is the slice clock inverted (transparent while the slice clock is low and GE is high)
meaning.not_inverted: the physical clock (or gate) is the slice clock
meaning.unknown: no attested reading: the configuration is outside the model's domain (no reading of v0.3 is unknown; the enum is kept so that the loader's domain mechanism and the marked v021_hole fixture of the tests keep working)

meaning.asynchronous: CLR / PRE, acting on the level
meaning.synchronous: R / S, acting at the edge

meaning.driven: SR driven from the slice input

meaning.latch: AFF..DFF are LDCE / LDPE; A5FF..D5FF are not storage elements

domain_refusal.executing_side_receives: a fixed refusal code, DOMAIN, carrying no reading, no semantic and no reason
never: a redraw condition of the search
an input to any decision in a session
domain_refusal.reason_available_through: the host-only diagnose() (unknown_readings), for audits and simulation reports
domain_refusal.status: a contract of the model and of every later tool (2b-2's cartographer and engine)

formal_input.rule: the committed file b4/hypothesis/ff_behaviour_v0.3.json, read by b4_ff_hypothesis.load() with no path and held to the digest pinned in that module, is the only formal hypothesis; any other document enters through fixture() / fixture_file(), verifies no source, and is marked fixture = true in every trace it produces; the superseded b4/hypothesis/ff_behaviour_v0.2.json is kept byte for byte (sha256 1118bedf4831bac3806be4aa3d9b56630912a946156869807f2c26f6374e6ed2) as the record of 0.2.1 and is a fixture like any other document (the tests' v021_hole)

initialisation_event.allowed_context: the slice clock low and the SR input de-asserted (docs/b4_architecture.md section 5.1 step 2); an init step in any other context is refused by the model
initialisation_event.assumption: sets Q := INIT on every applicable element and clears nothing else; modelled on the UNISIM GSR. A MODEL ABSTRACTION: the assignment is atomic and the init step settles no level effect — a latch whose gate is open at the init step (v0.3: the slice clock low under the inverted-gate reading) still reads INIT at the init readout; the first set step then settles at the old clock level before the clock changes (b4_ff_model)
initialisation_event.status: unverified; A8 of docs/b4_architecture.md section 5.5 (which event restores INIT on the board) is still unresolved

executing_side_visible: edge (rising | falling | null) of the slice clock
ce, sr, d (one bit per element, as applied)
q_before, q_after per element (0 | 1 | null = no readout given by the hypothesis for that element in that configuration, or never initialised)
host_only_diagnostics: the decode per element (primitive, INIT, SRVAL, CE / SR modes, kind, inversion)
the physical edge per element per step
observation_context.status: the executing side (the board, the cartographer, the search) sees only the first list; the second is derived from the decode and is for the host's audit and simulation reports, never an input to a decision in a session

primitive_selection.rule: by (storage_kind, sr_kind, SRVAL): flip-flop + synchronous + SRVAL 0 -> FDRE; + SRVAL 1 -> FDSE; flip-flop + asynchronous + SRVAL 0 -> FDCE; + SRVAL 1 -> FDPE; latch + SRVAL 0 -> LDCE; latch + SRVAL 1 -> LDPE (a latch's SR is always asynchronous; sr_kind is not applicable to a latch)

items: the bit readings in `decode` (machine enums; the human meaning beside each)

clock_mode read by storage context: flip-flop — bit 1 inverted; latch — bit 1 NOT inverted (the attested LDCE endpoint of docs/ff_latch_probe.md), bit 0 inverted (the D1' host correspondence pair, v0.3); three layers kept apart: L1 the host endpoint correspondence (the repository_document sources), L2 the vendor's primitive behaviour (the vendor_primitive sources), L3 the project's generalisation assumptions G1-G6 below
the pin correspondence: the slice clock is C (or G for a latch), CE is CE (or GE), SR is R / S / CLR / PRE by the decoded kind and value

the initialisation event of the carrier is modelled as the UNISIM GSR, taken with the slice clock low and SR de-asserted: every applicable element takes its INIT — whether the carrier's event does so on silicon is condition A8 of docs/b4_architecture.md section 5.5

G1 (v0.3) the other bits do not change the reading: CLKINV under a latch means the same for every assignment of the other 19 bits, although the D1' pair held them fixed (INIT 0, SRVAL 0 -> LDCE, CE and CLR driven, four main elements, the x5FF elements empty)

G2 (v0.3) the property is the behaviour: the bitstream bit that corresponds to the resolved IS_G_INVERTED property is realised on silicon as the slice-level clock inversion — the same mechanism CLKINV encodes for a flip-flop; nothing on silicon has been observed

G3 (v0.3) the vendor's simulation model describes the silicon gate: G_in = G xor IS_G_INVERTED and the UDP table of LDCE.v / LDPE.v (the standing premise of every vendor_primitive source, applied to one more configuration)

G4 (v0.3) the correspondence is tool- and recipe-invariant: the pair was built once, under Vivado 2025.2 and one recipe (two attempts, identical readbacks); other tool versions, anchors or occupations are not attested

G5 (v0.3) the per-slice reading: four main elements speak for the slice-level bit (clock_mode is per slice in the certificate mapping), and the x5FF elements, not storage elements under a latch, carry no reading of their own

G6 (v0.3) the initialisation context: with the gate inverted the slice clock low at the init step means the gate is OPEN; the init readout still shows INIT only because the model's init step assigns INIT atomically and settles nothing (initialisation_event); which event restores INIT on the board is A8, unresolved

valid_configuration.rule: an assignment of the 21 bits is in the model's domain when every decoded reading is known; in v0.3 every reading of every semantic in both storage contexts is known, so every assignment of the 21 bits is in the domain — the assignments with LATCH = 1 and CLKINV = 0 (19 free bits, 2^19 assignments) that v0.2 refused are in it under the v0.3 latch reading
valid_configuration.status: a domain definition for the model (v0.3); the completeness of the domain rests on the v0.3 latch reading — one host correspondence pair, the vendor's simulation model and the named assumptions G1-G6 — and on no observation; not a statement that any configuration is legal to build, safe to write, or observed; the DOMAIN refusal remains the contract for any reading a later revision declares unknown
